text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Desmond Choo –

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The FDW might also not earn enough to repay the agency fees or loans she had taken in order to come to Singapore to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Families caring for the elderly and who require short-term care options can also tap on respite care services available at senior care centres or nursing homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For younger children, families may engage childcare centres or student care centres on a suitable care arrangement that meets their needs, which may also include short-term care.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One, why is the Work Permit for FDWs fixed at two years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will MOM consider reviewing this permit term duration?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second question is, I find HSS rather interesting, rather novel, but it is currently confined only to cleaning services.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can MOM actually consider extending this pilot scheme to, perhaps, caregiving as well, that is, for households requiring caregiving services?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This takes into consideration the resources and also the efforts that both the FDW and the employer invest in the employment relationship.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, the FDW needs time for her to earn enough to repay the fee that needs to be paid to the employment agency.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Also, the employer also needs time to train the FDW.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, that is why it is set at a two-year period.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I just ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether we can consider providing some subsidies for HSS?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a similar way that we provide subsidies for the foreign worker levy, can we consider such subsidies also for HSS?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Louis Ng for the question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And as we review how we can improve HSS, we need to bear in mind how we are designing it to provide the support for sandwich families where they have younger kids and the elderly.
